header.title: Papyrus Ebers: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Medical papyri
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawmedizin:papyrus-ebers:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.1.5: 1.5: ṯs.w 'utterances, spells'; s,t-ꜥ, lit. 'action of the hand', is the harmful influence of a being; ḥmw,t-rʾ, lit. 'craft of the mouth', is a hostile spell; srḫ,y 'accuser'; bjbj unidentified. 1.17: sn 'brother', as written. 1.19: dšr 'red', the colour of harm. 1.20: jꜣbt.t is unclear, perhaps for jbṯ,t 'trap'.
notes.1.26: 1.26: ḥmw,t-rʾ, lit. 'craft of the mouth', a hostile spell. 1.32: jz,t, here 'hall', is uncertain. 2.1 is a bare numeral, probably a page or column number.
notes.5.248: swj,t: probably a suppository or pellet, given the next line. ḥkꜣ,pl 'magic', here an affliction caused by magic, or the name of a disease. jm,j n 'what is in', perhaps the pith or contents. ḥmm, wḏꜥyt and šnj-tꜣ ('earth-hair') are unidentified plants or drugs. sntr (incense) and its 1 are written above the line. The 1 after each ingredient is a quantity, probably one part.
notes.5.257: ḥkꜣ,pl 'magic', here an affliction caused by magic, or the name of a disease.
notes.5.261: ḥkꜣ,pl 'magic', here an affliction caused by magic. ꜥꜣꜥ: 'seed, emission' or 'poison'.
notes.41.50: 41.51: r mn.t =s, perhaps 'for her ailment' (mn 'suffer') or 'up to her thighs' (mn,t). 41.53: hbj is read as 'ibis'. 41.56: jrt,t is taken as jrṯ,t, 'milk'. 41.57: wꜥḥ is probably the earth almond (tiger nut); nꜥgw is unclear, perhaps 'roasted' or 'crushed'.

nodes.text: Mine are the spells that the Lord of All made to drive out the influence of a god, a goddess, a dead man, a dead woman, [and] the curse that is in this head of mine, in this neck of mine, in these shoulders of mine, in this flesh of mine, in these limbs of mine; to punish the accuser, the chief of those who bring disturbance into this flesh of mine and *bjbj* into these limbs of mine, as what enters into this flesh of mine, into this head of mine, into these shoulders of mine, into this body of mine, into these limbs of mine.
I belong to Ra; he has said:
'It is I who will protect him from his enemies.'
His guide is Thoth.
He makes writing speak,
he makes the compendia,
he gives effectiveness to the learned and to the physicians who are in his following, to loosen the one whom the god loves, that he may keep him alive.
I am one whom the god loves; he will keep me alive.
Words to be spoken when applying a remedy to any limb of a man that is ailing.
Truly effective, a million times.
Another spell, for loosening every bandage.
Loosened, loosened by Isis!
Horus was loosened by Isis from the evils done to him by his brother Seth when he killed his father Osiris.
O Isis, great of magic, may you loosen me,

may you release me from every bad, evil, red thing, from the influence of a god, the influence of a goddess, from a dead man, a dead woman, from a male adversary, a female adversary, who will oppose himself in me, as you loosened, as you released your son Horus; for I have entered into the fire, I have come out of the water.
I will not fall into the trap(?) of this day.
Now you have rescued me from every bad, evil, red thing, from the influence of a god, the influence of a goddess, from a dead man, a dead woman, [and] a curse.
Truly effective, a million times.
Spell for drinking a remedy.
Come, remedy!
Come, you who drive out the thing in this heart of mine, in these limbs of mine!
Magic is strong through the remedy, and vice versa.
Do you remember that Horus and Seth were taken to the great hall of Heliopolis, when inquiry was made into the testicles of Seth together with [the Eye of] Horus?
Then he will flourish, as he is on earth;
he will do all that he wishes, like those gods who are there.
Words to be spoken while drinking a remedy.
Truly effective, a million times.
Beginning of the compendium of remedies for driving out illness from the belly.
Make into a *swjt*;
put [it] into the anus for 4 days.
Driving out magic from the belly:
inner part of *ḥmm*, 1; inner part of *wḏꜥyt*, 1; incense, 1; *šnj-tꜣ*, 1; sweet beer.
Rub [them] together into one mass.
Another, for driving out magic from the belly of a man or a woman.
Another, for driving out magic, the *ꜥꜣꜥ* of a god or of a dead man, from the belly of a man.
The woman's fingers are rubbed with them;
then you shall put it on all her limbs for her ailment(?).
Another, for making the womb go down to its place:
an ibis of wax;
put [it] on charcoal;
let its smoke enter her flesh.
Examining good milk:
its smell is like *nꜥgw* of *wꜥḥ*.
